newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms on low dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms on low dollar demand.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev firmed to around 1,650-1,740 per dollar around 1100 local time (0800 GMT) from the opening levels of 1,750-1,950 because foreign currency demand was lower than expected, dealers said.
"The expected rush on the dollar following a main (lev) interest rate cut has not materialised yet," a commercial bank dealer said.

Trade was calm and the bid/ask spreads for the dollar narrowed to around 60-90 levs from 150-200 levs in opening quotes but there was an underlying nervousness in the market and the lev could easily slip, dealers said.
The central bank cut its main interest rate to 4.29 percent monthly from 5.20 percent, effective from Monday. It was not seen supporting the lev.
The lev slumped to around 1,685-1,700 per dollar at close on Friday from the opening's 1,543-1,545 due to a massive shortcovering after the central bank said it would cut its main interest rate.

The cut was expected to pare further yields on lev-denominated, floating interest government securities, which have attracted foreign investors since March, when the main interest rate stood at 18 percent monthly.
Those investors were a major source of foreign currency supply in the past two months but they were not seen on the local forex market on Monday, dealers said.
Interest on local floating interest T-bills is pegged to the main interest rate and falls with each rate cut during the period to maturity.
